reason: The support cells' curled membrane sheets suggest they wrap around and insulate the motor neuron fibers.
expectation: The support cells will insulate the outgoing nerve fibers.

effect: The support cells wrapped the motor fibers, completing the insulated nerve routes; the next goal is to connect sight to muscle commands.
reaction: The segmented wrapping and gaps are a useful detail.
reason: The eyes detect the scene, and the sensory nerves appear to carry information toward a central connection.
expectation: The sensory nerves will connect to the eyes to carry visual information.

effect: The eyes and sensory nerves formed a visual information route; it still needs a central connection to reach muscle commands.
reaction: The change from light rays to a nerve signal makes the route clearer.
reason: The central nervous system appears to be the next connection for incoming visual information.
expectation: The visual route will connect to the brain and spinal cord.

effect: The visual route connected to the central nervous system, forming a seeing control system that identifies the target's location.
reaction: The distinction between seeing the target and producing force is clear.
reason: The seeing control system needs an outgoing route to send commands toward the muscles.
expectation: The motor nerves will connect the control system to an outgoing command route.

effect: The motor nerves now extend from the control system, but their muscle endings are still unattached.
reaction: The unattached endings make the next connection clear.
reason: The outgoing motor nerves need to connect to the arm muscles to carry commands to them.
expectation: The motor nerve endings will connect to the arm muscles.

effect: The control system and arm are connected, completing the sight-to-command route; the remaining goal is to return information about arm position.
reaction: The incoming and outgoing arrows make the connection easy to follow.
reason: The stretch receptors sit among muscle fibers and their sensory nerves carry signals back, matching the new goal.
expectation: The receptors and sensory nerves will connect the arm to the central nervous system to report its position.

effect: The receptors completed the return route, showing how arm-position information can reach the central nervous system even with the eyes closed.
reaction: The eyes-closed example made the purpose of position feedback concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the stretch receptors was most worthwhile because it connected the returning sensory signal to a familiar experience: knowing where an arm is without looking at it.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the motor nerves to the control system felt predictable after the preceding steps, though it clearly prepared the route to the muscles.

surprise.text: The segmented support-cell wrapping, with gaps between segments, added a detail I had not expected from the initial pieces.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt particularly arbitrary; the item descriptions and goals gave each connection a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because the constructions made the links between sensory information, nerve signals and muscle action understandable, and I am curious how the next body system will connect to them.
